subject: Private deployment: customer keys, subprocessors, and transfer windows
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@aureliahealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment: initial DPA questions on keys & transfers

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — our infra and legal teams reconvened and have a handful of specific questions before we move to procurement. We're evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) and need clarity on three items so we can align our DPA:  

1) Customer-managed keys: We need to confirm whether customer keys can be placed in our Azure Key Vault (customer-controlled) and whether Redwood will ever have a key escrow/equivalent for emergency operator access. If so, what triggers that access and what logging/evidence is produced?

2) Subprocessors and operator network access: Aurelia requires a list of subprocessors and a statement about whether Redwood operators (or contractors) will be able to access the private deployment host network or the model artifacts. If operator access is possible, what scopes are used (console-only, SSH jump, vm-access)?

3) Cross-border transfer windows: Our data retention policy forbids any unencrypted customer content to leave EEA. Please confirm where inference telemetry, logs, and any temporary artifacts may flow (control plane vs data plane). Do you offer geofenced control plane options or a private control plane entirely within our VNet?

Can you please send proposed DPA language and any runbook or evidence we can attach to our internal security review? We have a tight calendar: procurement expects a redline by 3/10.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Senior Counsel, Aurelia Health
elena.morris@aureliahealth.com
Attachment: Aurelia-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX)
From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T10:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment: initial DPA questions on keys & transfers

Elena — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Karthik (infra/security engineer) and Marissa (privacy/compliance) who can add precise language and evidence. High-level answers while they draft redlines:  

- Customer-managed keys: supported. Customer can use Azure Key Vault (or on-prem HSM/KMS) and Redwood will accept customer-provided key material for at-rest encryption of model caches and for TLS termination where applicable. We do have an optional emergency key-escrow workflow for break-glass that requires a documented approval chain (customer POA + Redwood security approval) and produces cryptographic audit logs and an immutable ticket (see attached draft redlines).

- Operator access: default deployment mode is operator-less day-to-day. Operators can be granted time-limited access for maintenance under an explicitly agreed escalation policy. Access types are limited to operator console sessions or jump-host sessions with strict session recording — we do not provide persistent SSH-level access to customer VM disks unless explicitly contracted in the Private Addendum.

- Cross-border flows: Data plane stays in customer VNet for VPC deployments; telemetry (aggregated anonymized metrics) can be routed to Redwood-hosted observability unless you opt out. We can offer a private control plane in-customer-VNet (private-controlplane option) to eliminate control-plane egress.

I'm attaching a first-pass DPA redline and will follow up with Karthik/Marissa for the runbook and SOC excerpt.

Next steps: Karthik/Marissa — can you draft two short option clauses for customer-managed keys (1. No escrow, customer sole custody; 2. Escrow with dual-approval + recorded access) and a short operator-access matrix we can share with Aurelia? Procurement needs redlines by 3/10.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Attachment: dpa_redlines_rachel_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, Elena Morris <elena.morris@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment: initial DPA questions on keys & transfers

Rachel / Elena — added technical context and a short runbook attached. Key points from engineering:  

- Customer KMS patterns: we support (a) Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) with Azure Key Vault using Managed HSM and RBAC-bound service principals; (b) On-prem HSM with PKCS#11 bridge; (c) Customer-supplied wrapping keys. In all cases, Redwood's runtime never persistently stores unencrypted plaintext keys — only wrapped key blobs.

- Escrow break-glass: if customer opts in, escrow keys are stored in a dual-control escrow (two-person approval) within a hardened HSM. Access triggers we accept: legal subpoena with court order OR customer-approved emergency request (signed POA). All break-glass operations are recorded to our WORM audit log and an automated notification is sent to the customer's security contact.

- Operator scopes: three discrete roles: Operator-Read (logs/metrics console read-only), Operator-Maintain (time-limited support sessions via recorded jump-host), and Operator-Admin (rare; requires contract addendum and is subject to additional safeguards). We explicitly exclude persistent root-level access to customer-managed keystores unless specified in the SLA addendum.

- Data flows: for VPC deployments, inference data and KV cache remain in-customer-subnet. Control-plane messages (deployment orchestration, health checks) can be brokered through a private-controlplane option. Telemetry is configurable; by default we collect only aggregated latency/error metrics unless the customer enables more detailed tracing.

I've attached a short runbook (privdep_kms_runbook_karthik.docx) and sample DPA snippets for the two escrow options Rachel requested. Happy to jump on a quick call with Aurelia's infra team if helpful.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: privdep_kms_runbook_karthik.docx (DOCX)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, Elena Morris <elena.morris@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-05T11:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment: initial DPA questions on keys & transfers

Elena / Team — from a privacy and legal perspective, here are the items we'd like in the DPA to keep procurement happy:  

1) Explicit statement that customer data (inference inputs/outputs) will remain in-customer VNet and not be indexed for model training.
2) Enumerated subprocessor list with 30-day notice for changes; ability to object and require an alternative subprocessor or onshore-only subprocessors for EU customers.
3) Clear operator access SLA: time-limited, recorded, dual-approval for any decryption event. Provide sample audit output (SOC2 excerpt) as evidence.
4) Cross-border clause: if control plane egress is necessary, Redwood will provide geofencing guarantees and signatory acceptance to local data transfer annotations (we recommend the private-controlplane option for EU-only requirement).

I attached a SOC2 excerpt (SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf) and proposed DPA language. For procurement: propose three options to include in the contract exhibit so Aurelia can pick one quickly:  
  A. Full BYOK (no escrow) — fastest to approve.
  B. BYOK + Escrow (dual-approval) — moderate governance, additional review.
  C. BYOK + On-prem control plane (no egress) — higher cost, strongest guarantee.

If Aurelia selects B or C, we'll also put in place a quarterly operator access attestation and a signed audit retention schedule.

Marissa Cole
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf (PDF)
From: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@aureliahealth.com>, procure@aureliahealth.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-06T16:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment: customer options and next steps (DPA redlines attached)

Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached are the redlines and three contract options (A/B/C) and a short summary table below to assist your procurement/legal team in selecting quickly. If you prefer, we can prepare a single marked DocuSign bundle for your signature after you choose an option.

Summary:  
- Option A (Full BYOK, no escrow): quickest; no escrow access; customer remains sole key custodian; recommended when Aurelia's ops can own key rotation.
- Option B (BYOK + Escrow dual-approval): Redwood stores escrow wrapped key in a dual-control HSM; break-glass requires customer POA + Redwood security sign-off; WORM audit logs provided; quarterly attestation.
- Option C (BYOK + Private control-plane): No control-plane egress; all orchestration endpoints deployed into customer VNet; operator access is console-only and fully recorded; higher setup fee.

Attachments: dpa_redlines_rachel_v1.pdf; privdep_kms_runbook_karthik.docx; SOC2_excerpt_2026.pdf
